facts.statement: Sisteronia is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur from the Middle Cretaceous of southeastern England and France.
facts.quote: Sisteronia is an extinct genus of platypterygiine ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur known from the 'middle' Cretaceous of southeastern England and southeastern France.

facts.statement: The genus Sisteronia was named by Fischer, Bardet, Guiomar, and Godefroit in 2014.
facts.quote: Sisteronia was named by Valentin Fischer, Nathalie Bardet, Myette Guiomar and Pascal Godefroit in 2014

facts.statement: The genus name honors the commune of Sisteron in southeastern France, where relatively complete specimens were collected.
facts.quote: The generic name honors Sisteron, a commune in the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, southeastern France, where relatively complete specimens referable to Sisteronia were collected

facts.statement: The holotype of Sisteronia is specimen CAMSM B58257_67, designated by Fischer et al. in 2014.
facts.quote: Fischer et al. (2014) designated CAMSM B58257_67 as the holotype of Sisteronia.

facts.statement: Sisteronia has three unique traits that distinguish it from all other known platypterygiine ophthalmosaurids.
facts.quote: Sisteronia possesses three autapomorphies, unique traits, that differentiate it from all other currently known platypterygiine ophthalmosaurids.

facts.statement: Based on its delicate, slender, and unworn teeth, Sisteronia likely preyed on soft-bodied small prey like small fish and neocoleoid cephalopods.
facts.quote: As suggested by its delicate, slender and unworn teeth, Sisteronia preyed on soft and small prey such as small fishes and neocoleoid cephalopods.

facts.statement: Fischer et al. assigned Sisteronia to the subfamily Platypterygiinae because it shares traits with that group and lacks traits of ophthalmosaurine ophthalmosaurids.
facts.quote: Fischer et al. (2013) assigned Sisteronia to Platypterygiinae as it possesses several synapomorphies of this clade and lacks the synapomorphies of ophthalmosaurine ophthalmosaurids.

facts.statement: Sisteronia lived from the Albian to the Cenomanian stages, between 113.2 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Cenomanian (113.2 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sisteronia belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae.
Sisteronia is classified within the infraorder Thunnosauria.

rejected.statement: The species name seeleyi honors British paleontologist Harry Govier Seeley, who cataloged thousands of fragmentary ichthyosaur specimens from the Cambridge Greensand Member.
rejected.quote: The specific name, seeleyi, honors the renowned British paleontologist Harry Govier Seeley who cataloged thousands fragmentary ichthyosaur specimens from the Cambridge Greensand Member of the Lower Chalk Formation.
